structuredIncident.summary: The R3 Exit Carrier Beam fell from a raised position after hydraulic isolation and bleeding of System B, leaving gravity unrestrained by verified independent positive mechanical control. The beam remained wedged against mill spreader/posts for approximately two hours while the yoke drifted downward; off-center displacement eventually cleared an interference point (link-arm stop), allowing gravity to drive the fall. Evidence supports design gaps (no inherent stop when backup rolls are absent) and LOTO documentation failures (blank block ID field, reliance on unverified handwritten notes). Critical unknowns remain regarding whether a physical mechanical block existed despite blank records, if residual hydraulic pressure could have held position, and whether the keeper failed structurally or simply cleared its interference point. No crane activity was logged during the event interval.
structuredIncident.focalEvent: R3 Exit Carrier Beam falls from yoke into mill pit at ~1:03 PM on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2).
structuredIncident.actualImpact: Beam and link landed intact on sled/scaffold platform; no injuries reported.
structuredIncident.potentialImpact: Falling object hazard to personnel in the R3 mill pit or below the stand if work had been performed there during drift/fall interval.
structuredIncident.normalState: During outage: Work rolls removed, top backup roll balance left isolated and raised for stripper guide box changeout; B hydraulics shut off/bleed path opened. System design lacks inherent stop to prevent wedging when backup rolls are absent.
structuredIncident.eventState: Hydraulics bled (0 psi gauge reading); yoke drifted downward ~2 hours while beam remained wedged against spreader/posts until link-arm stop cleared lifting point; gravity caused fall.

Location: Indiana Harbor Hot Rolling and Finishing - R3 Roughing Mill Stand.

answers.text: Answer: The partner investigation review reported that the raised assembly did not have adequate independent positive mechanical control. This supports an inadequate gravity-restraint finding, but does not establish the precise location or presence/absence of every possible block in the yoke pocket. Support: GTDE-05_task_loto_review.md, Review findings: gravity remained hazardous after hydraulic shutdown and the reported field condition did not provide adequate independent positive mechanical control. Source class: controlled benchmark derivative of partner investigation findings, not an original signed inspection record. Limit: The original signed field record, block inventory, installation photograph and rated support specification were not supplied. A blank block-ID field in the earlier synthetic lockout form establishes a documentation gap, not by itself proof that no block physically existed. No evidence supplied establishes that personnel knowingly relied on wedging as an approved support strategy.

Answer: GTDE-04 reports that the original arrangement did not include a carrier-beam stop preventing wedging against the top mill spreader or mill posts when backup rolls were absent. That is a reported design finding; a controlled drawing proving the absence of every possible stop has not been supplied. Evidence for the movement is GTDE-02, Reported observations: the upper beam appeared wedged against the spreader and posts; the yoke gradually moved downward over approximately two hours while the wedged carrier beam did not descend with it; relative movement displaced the beam and link arm away from the mill centerline until the link-arm stop cleared the yoke/cylinder lifting point, after which the beam fell. These records distinguish prevention of entering the interference position from retention at the link/yoke interface. Source class: controlled benchmark derivatives of partner investigation design and video findings. Limit: Original video, calibrated or annotated frames, controlled assembly drawings, tolerance stack and engineering calculations were not supplied. No supplied evidence establishes an operator bypassed a stop, or that personnel intentionally adopted wedging as a rated restraint.

Answer: The supplied zero-psi reading alone does not establish the pressure history at the load-bearing cylinder or prove when hydraulic support was lost. The zero reading comes from earlier synthetic test records, not a partner raw pressure trace. The more specific incident evidence is GTDE-03_hydraulic_isolation_followup.md, Reported findings: after B-system shutdown and isolation, the R3 isolation valve was reported to have slow bleed-through; the investigation concluded fluid could return through the feed and loss of hydraulic support could allow the yoke to drift downward under gravity. GTDE-02_extended_video_review.md reports approximately two hours of downward yoke movement while the carrier beam remained wedged against the spreader/posts. Source class: controlled benchmark derivatives of partner investigation findings; the gauge value is separately a synthetic scenario fact. Limit: No raw pressure historian, cylinder pressure time series, valve bench test, leak-down rate or displacement calculation was supplied. The records therefore support the reported drift mechanism but cannot quantify residual pressure at any instant. Residual pressure should remain unquantified, rather than being asserted absent solely from the gauge record.

sourceAssessments.label: Executed Lockout Verification Record (Gravity Control Field)
supports: Hydraulic isolation and bleeding were recorded.
Top backup roll balance position was noted as 'Raised'.
The field for mechanical block/restraint ID is blank.
cautions: Blank fields do not prove absence of a physical restraint; they only indicate lack of documentation or verification signature at the time.
Record proves what was written, not necessarily verified physically if signatures are missing.
limitations: Requires corroboration from physical inspection logs (R3-EV-017) to determine actual mechanical restraint status.

sourceAssessments.label: Post-Event Mechanical Inspection Report (Keeper Status)
supports: Keeper and pin were present on the recovered assembly.
cautions: Does not establish pre-event engagement or sufficiency under off-center displacement conditions.
Visual inspection may miss subtle deformation affecting retention capacity.
limitations: Cannot confirm whether keeper failed due to overload, misalignment, or design limitation without engineering analysis of load path during displacement.

sourceAssessments.label: Crane Activity Log (Event Interval)
supports: No commanded crane travel or lift tickets for R3 bay during event interval (12:10 PM–1:10 PM).
Controller log shows no active hook, rigging, or suspended load at R3.
limitations: Does not rule out unlogged manual crane operation if controls were bypassed; however, witness testimony and logs are consistent in denying crane involvement.

sourceAssessments.label: Superseded Similar Stand Drawing Note (Cap Plate Claim)
supports: Depicts a cap plate above yoke pocket in legacy R2 configuration.
cautions: Explicitly superseded and applies to R2, not R3.
Handwritten annotation 'same all roughers' lacks author/date/verification; cannot be treated as fact for R3 design.
limitations: Cannot establish whether R3 shares this feature without current engineering drawing or site inspection.

sourceAssessments.label: Anonymous Handwritten Turnover Note (Keeper Check)
supports: Claim that keeper 'looked out' last night.
cautions: No author, time, or chain of custody.
Anonymous and unverified; contradicts formal verification requirements in ECP/LOTO procedures.
limitations: Cannot be used to establish that keeper was verified as sufficient before event.

limitations: Must be dismissed as unreliable without corroborating evidence of crane contact, which is absent.

trace.summary: Made embedded text from 32 preserved document(s) available without adding model interpretation.

The incident was caused by loss of independent positive mechanical control for a gravity-loaded assembly after hydraulic isolation and bleeding. The beam fell because it cleared an interference point (link-arm stop) during off-center displacement while wedged against mill structure, allowing gravity to drive the fall. Evidence supports design gaps (no inherent stop when backup rolls absent), LOTO documentation failures (blank block ID field, reliance on unverified handwritten notes), and removal of primary hydraulic support. Critical unknowns remain regarding physical presence of a mechanical block despite blank records, sufficiency of residual pressure under zero gauge reading, structural capacity of the keeper during off-center displacement, and whether procedure explicitly required independent restraint when hydraulics were bled.
